Text   serialization:   why   it   fails   for   relational   learning 
11 
Lost   “cell”   semantics 
numerical :   LLM   tokenizer   chops   the   number   800.00   into   text   pieces   (e.g.,   ["800",   “.00”]) 
categorical :   keys/categorical   IDs   like   C1   or   I4   mean   nothing   to   a   standard   ML   model 
temporal :   Treating   2023-12-31   and   2024-01-01   as   strings   makes   them   look   entirely   different   to   an   LLM 
NULL :   standard   tokenizer   loses   typed   missingness   behavior   (unknown,   n/a,   WITHHELD,   ERR,   etc)

The   Permutation   Problem 
Row-level   model   returns   one   prediction   per   row 
example:   predict   whether   each   invoice   is   fraudulent 
Table-level   model   returns   one   output   for   the   whole   table 
example:   classify   the   whole   table   or   compute   one   table   embedding 
Practical   implication: 
If   a   model   changes   its   answer   just   because   a   CSV   was   exported   in   a   different   row   order   or   a   schema   was 
serialized   in   a   different   column   order,   then   it   has   learned   a   formatting   artifact,   not   table   semantics. 
In   relations   row   and   column   order   are   not   semantics

=== PDF PAGE 47 ===
Standard   inference:   understands   the   question   retrieve   relevant   evidence   produce   an   answer 
Over   a   live   database,   answering   a   question   may   additionally   require: 
semantic   retrieval:   vague   or   text-heavy   matching,   e.g.,   fi nd   ``complaints   about   billing   fraud’' 
exact   execution:   compute   joins,   counts,   sums,   fi lters,   and   time   windows   (SQL) 
schema   grounding:   identify   which   tables,   columns,   and   join   paths   are   relevant 
integrity:   respect   foreign   keys,   valid   joins,   and   permissions 
answer   synthesis:   turn   rows   or   aggregates   into   a   useful   explanation 
freshness   and   provenance:   answer   currency   and   provenance   (evidence)

Vector   RAG :   solves   semantic   evidence   retrieval 
The   common   RAG   architecture:   embedding-based   semantic   retrieval   for   LLM   context 
Relational   RAG :   solves   exact   structured   execution   based   retrieval 
Use   SQL   queries   to   retrieve   results   as   fi nal   answers   or   LLM   context 
key   interface:   NL2SQL 
Table-augmented   Retrieval   (TAG) :   solves   hybrid   questions,   both   exact   execution   and   explanation 
Mix   of   vector   and   relational   RAG 
RAG   extended   for   relational   databases

=== PDF PAGE 49 ===
NL2SQL   is   ideal   when   a   question   can   be   answered   by: 
selecting   the   right   tables   and   columns, 
forming   the   right   joins, 
applying   the   right   fi lters, 
executing   exact   aggregation   in   the   DB   engine. 
Core   abstraction 
NL2SQL   maps   a   natural-language   question   to   SQL;   the   DBMS   then   executes   the   SQL 
Retrieve   structured   evidence   units   such   as   rows,   joined   rows,   entities,   paths,   or   attached   documents 
rigrous   semantics,   exactness,   no   approximation/vagueness/hallucination 
NL2SQL   —   the   exact-execution   interface   of   relational   RAG
